answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by capping the trust that flows through any single introducer: a newcomer gains standing only when an established agent vouches for it, and each voucher's total backing is capped, so a thousand fake identities hanging off one sponsor share one thin slice of trust, like meltwater from a single glacier feeding many streams but never becoming a river. Genuine agents branch outward across many independent sponsors, widening their horizon, while a farm's copies cluster under one roof and draw only nectar-thin support each.
